objectives: Assess neonatal eye discharge with systemic danger-sign screening.
Differentiate local conjunctival infection from neonatal sepsis risk.
Start appropriate local care including erythromycin eye ointment and referral when severe signs appear.
takeaways: In neonates, poor feeding, fever/hypothermia, and lethargy can signal systemic infection.
Purulent eye discharge with swollen lids may need both local treatment and close follow-up.
Erythromycin eye ointment and hygienic eye care are practical first-line actions when stable.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A 6-day-old newborn presents with sticky eye discharge. Decide if this is local infection or a wider neonatal danger pattern.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Eye discharge and eyelid swelling in newborn

sections.title: Mother's report
sections.text: Discharge started yesterday. Baby still breastfeeds but less vigorously.

coach.title: Baby Nambi is only 6 days old
coach.body: Neonates can deteriorate quickly. Always screen systemic danger signs before local treatment.

sections.title: Neonatal danger signs
sections.reveal_note: No convulsions or chest indrawing; feeding slightly reduced.

coach.title: What is your best immediate interpretation?
coach.body: Use both local eye findings and systemic neonatal signs.

question.prompt: How should you classify this presentation now?

options.text: Possible neonatal conjunctivitis; treat locally and monitor closely for systemic illness
Harmless blocked tear duct only, no follow-up required
Meningitis confirmed from eye discharge alone
No treatment needed in neonates with eye pus

question.right: Correct. Current findings support localized neonatal eye infection, but age 6 days requires strict safety-net and close review.
question.wrong: In neonates, minimizing infection signs is risky. Eye discharge can be local now but can progress if follow-up is poor.

sections.title: Initial treatment
sections.detail: Apply to affected eye(s) per protocol with gentle saline cleansing

sections.title: Urgent return triggers
sections.reveal_note: Mother demonstrates cleaning technique and return plan.

coach.title: Choose the safest newborn care plan
coach.body: Pick the action that balances treatment and escalation vigilance.

options.text: Start erythromycin eye ointment, teach eye hygiene, and arrange very early review
Give only herbal eye wash and wait one week
Delay all treatment until lab culture is available
Use steroid eye drops as first-line therapy

question.right: Correct. Early topical therapy plus strict neonatal follow-up is appropriate when systemic danger signs are not yet present.
question.wrong: Delaying treatment or using inappropriate drops can worsen neonatal eye infection and risk systemic spread.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You treated likely neonatal conjunctivitis and gave high-quality newborn safety-net counseling.
sections.emphasis: Neonatal age itself increases risk and follow-up urgency.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: In newborn eye complaints, always pair local treatment with systemic danger-sign screening. Erythromycin ointment and caregiver coaching are practical first actions when the infant is currently stable.
